title: Stop workers with CancellationToken and wait with TaskTracker
summary: An AtomicBool cannot wake a worker asleep for 30 seconds, and main exits first. Race cancelled() in select!, hang on a TaskTracker nobody closed, and stop only the mailer with child_token.

turns.user: ctrl-c kills it without a single "billing: stopped". looks like jobs get cut mid way. i want it to actually stop and then exit

assistant.body: Great question! There are two causes. First, main returns right after setting stop, and leaving main tears down the runtime, so the workers never get to finish. Second, a worker does not look at the flag during its 30 second sleep. Switching to CancellationToken from tokio_util puts cancelled().await on one side of a select!, so a sleeping worker wakes and breaks the moment cancel is called. cancelled is cancel safe, so losing the select! and being dropped is fine. Spawning through a TaskTracker and awaiting tracker.wait() after token.cancel() guarantees every worker prints stopped before the process ends.

turns.user: ok 3 stopped lines now. but then it just hangs. hitting ctrl-c again does nothing either

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous code never called tracker.close(). TaskTracker::wait returns only once the tracker is empty and closed. With every task done but the tracker still open, it keeps waiting for a spawn that never comes. The second Ctrl-C does nothing because once ctrl_c has been awaited, tokio owns the signal and the default exit no longer runs. close goes right after the last spawn.

turns.user: need to stop just the mailer when SMTP is down. via kill -USR1. ctrl-c should obviously still stop everything

assistant.body: Here's the split. The mailer gets a child token made with child_token from the root. Cancelling a child reaches neither the parent nor its siblings, while cancelling the parent reaches every child. So the Ctrl-C path stays as it was, and USR1 only touches the mailer. The task waiting on USR1 is not in the tracker, so wait will not hang on it.
